data_state.rationale: Filling logic through method or tolerance requires the DataFrame index to be monotonically increasing or decreasing. Also, original NaNs in data are preserved.

partitions.monotonic: DataFrame index is sorted and monotonically increasing or decreasing
partitions.non_monotonic: DataFrame index is not monotonically sorted

partitions.intersecting: New index partially overlaps with original index, keeping original values for matched labels
partitions.disjoint: New index has no overlap with original index
partitions.equivalent: New index is identical to original index

partitions.none: Default behavior with no gaps filled
partitions.ffill: Propagate last valid observation forward to next valid
partitions.bfill: Use next valid observation backward to fill gap

invalid_cases.desc: Using a method when the DataFrame index is not monotonically increasing or decreasing raises ValueError

partitions.default_nan: Missing values are filled with NaN
partitions.custom_value: Missing values are filled with a specific custom scalar like 0 or 'missing'

postconditions.claim: When no fill method is specified, labels in the new index that do not exist in the original index are filled with fill_value.
When the original index is not monotonic and a filling method is specified, a ValueError is raised.
When the original index is monotonic and a ffill method is specified, unmapped new labels are filled with the last valid observation.
postconditions.expected_behavior: result.loc[new_labels_not_in_original] reflects propagated values from previous index

postconditions.claim: When the new index is completely identical to the old index, the resulting DataFrame maintains the exact same data.
